title: the settings dialogs work but are hard to use, and GUI.py is hard to change
author: Claude-JG
description: python/exudyn/GUI.py does its job with tkinter - it runs everywhere and needs no installation - but it is in bad shape, and the dialogs are called from rendererPythonInterface.cpp, which executes Python inside C++. What the maintainer names (2026-09-22): the table of the visualization settings is restricted; illegal input is caught but there are no type hints; the font size cannot be adjusted on Linux; the columns can hardly be adjusted; a description should appear in a pop-up rather than only with a special key; fields cannot be edited inline; combo boxes are unhandy. Two things changed the ground under it: revision2026 step R4.10 makes the parameter TYPES available to Python, and the interface is generic enough that a second front end (Qt6, or a form that takes Qt5 and Qt6) would be a small overhead on top. A snapshot of the dialog as it is: docs/theDoc/figures/visualizationSettings.png in the history.
workingRemarks: REVIEWED 2026-09-22, written up in revision2026b step RG6.2. Each of the seven complaints has a cause in python/exudyn/misc/GUI.py (1017 lines): type and size are read into typeStorage/sizeStorage and never shown; CheckType reports an illegal value without naming the expected type; 'if not IsApple(): fontFactor = 1' forces the font factor to 1 off macOS and the setting is called dialogs.fontScalingMacOS; tree.column(...) is never called, so every column keeps the 200 px default; the description is bound to the key 'h' and shown in a modal messagebox; the value is edited in a separate Entry/Combobox at the bottom that swaps with the tree by z-order; GetComboBoxListsDict hard-codes three enum types, so timeIntegration.explicitIntegration.dynamicSolverType (a DynamicSolverType) is edited as free text. Two findings change the step: the dialog is NOT visualization-specific - GetDictionaryWithTypeInfo is bound for SimulationSettings too (152 editable values against 470, all with descriptions), so a solver settings dialog is a call that nothing offers rather than a new dialog; and 220 of the 775 lines of rendererPythonInterface.cpp ARE Python in raw strings, with the help dialog (69 lines) and the command window (93 lines) written in full inside the C++ where no linter, no stub check and no test ever sees them. Nothing calls any function of GUI.py in any test; the layer that can be tested without a window is ConvertString2Value / ConvertValue2String / CheckType / GetComboBoxListsDict.
